useEventBus.description:
Whether to use the event bus API in the events plugin backend to
distribute events across multiple instances when publishing and
subscribing to events.

The default is 'auto', which means means that the event bus API will be
used if it's available, but will be disabled if the events backend
returns a 404.

If set to 'never', the events service will only ever publish events
locally to the same instance, while if set to 'always', the event bus API
will never be disabled, even if the events backend returns a 404.

notifyTimeoutMs.description:
Timeout in milliseconds for how long to wait before closing subscription events
requests to ensure they don't stall or that events get stuck. Defaults to 55 seconds.

topics.description:
Topics for which a route has to be registered
at which we can receive events via HTTP POST requests
(i.e. received from webhooks).

auth.description: Configuration options for the auth plugin

providers.description: The available auth-provider options and attributes

userEntityRef.description: The entity reference to use for the guest user.

ownershipEntityRefs.description:
A list of entity references to user for ownership of the guest user if the user
 is not found in the catalog.

dangerouslyAllowOutsideDevelopment.description: Allow users to sign in with the guest provider outside of their development environments.

gcpIap.description: Configuration for the Google Cloud Platform Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) auth provider.

audience.description:
The audience to use when validating incoming JWT tokens.
See https://backstage.io/docs/auth/google/gcp-iap-auth

jwtHeader.description: The name of the header to read the JWT token from, defaults to `'x-goog-iap-jwt-assertion'`.

secret.description: The secret attribute of session object.

identityTokenAlgorithm.description:
JWS "alg" (Algorithm) Header Parameter value. Defaults to ES256.
Must match one of the algorithms defined for IdentityClient.
When setting a different algorithm, check if the `key` field
of the `signing_keys` table can fit the length of the generated keys.
If not, add a knex migration file in the migrations folder.
More info on supported algorithms: https://github.com/panva/jose

keyStore.description: To control how to store JWK data in auth-backend

ssl.description: Whether to use SSL when connecting.

keyFilename.description:
Local file containing the Service Account credentials.
You can omit this value to automatically read from
GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS env which is useful for local
development.

path.description: The path to use for the collection. Defaults to 'sessions'

timeout.description: Timeout used for database operations. Defaults to 10000ms

keys.description: Must be declared at least once and the first one will be used for signing

publicKeyFile.description: Path to the public key file in the SPKI format

privateKeyFile.description: Path to the matching private key file in the PKCS#8 format

keyId.description: id to uniquely identify this key within the JWK set

algorithm.description:
JWS "alg" (Algorithm) Header Parameter value. Defaults to ES256.
Must match the algorithm used to generate the keys in the provided files

experimentalExtraAllowedOrigins.description: Additional app origins to allow for authenticating
